newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate falls, baht eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate falls, baht eases late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate was slightly lower to 11.50-11.75 percent late on Thursday compared with 11.50-12.00 percent in the morning due to low demand for funds, dealers said.
"The overnight interbank rate fell amid a test by the Bank of Thailand following a speculation on the baht last week," said a dealer at Thai Danu Bank.
Dealers said they had heard that the central bank was trying to keep the interbank rate high in order to keep speculators away.
The baht fell to 25.563-25.567 to the dollar late from 25.539-25.542 in early morning on late dollar buying, prompting dealers to speculate that the central bank may soon intervene in the market.
The dealer from Thai Danu Bank said the buying of dollar was due to a lack of confidence in the stability of the baht among the players as there was still no sign of economic recovery.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was quoted at 8.50-9.50 satangs per a dollar late from 9.00 satangs in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.51 versus 25.54 on Wednesday.
